g.text: Topic: HTML
Date: 17 August 2025
Mentor: Sushant Goyal
Topics:
1. What is HTML
2. Basic Tags
3. div vs span
4. Semantic tags
5. Forms
6. Tables
HTML
HyperText Markup Language
HyperText - text which can jump to other pages
Markup Language - using tags to describe how content should appear
HTML is the building block of every web page
Invented by Tim Berners Lee in 1991
1. HTML is not case-sensitive. but prefer lowercase tags
<DIV> or <dIv>.
2. HTML 5 - the usage of semantic tags, multimedia inputs and improvements in forms
3. W3C - World Wide Web Consortium
Chrome - HTML Parser
Firefox - HTML Parser 2
Safari - HTML Parser 3
Edge - HTML Parser 4
<!DOCTYPE html>
lang attribute in html
1. information about the language for the document
2. it helps screen readers and assistive technologies to read content in correct language
3. It allows browser to apply correct locale based settings
DD-MM-YYYY
MM-DD-YYYY
DD-MMM-YYYY
Text block - p tag
Inline block - span tag
scope block - div tag
Defining a HTML Tag
Opening Tag:
Angle bracket open (<)
Tag Name (h1,h2,...,h6, p, div ...)
Angle bracket close (>)
Closing Tag
Angle bracket open (<)
Slash or terminator (/)
Tag name
Angle bracket close (>)
Div Tag:
1. Block level element used to group larger sections of the content
2. It takes up full width of the container, meaning it will start from a new line
and stretches over the complete page
Use Cases:
1. When we need to group the content together into separate section or areas
2. For layout designing,
Span tag:
1. Inline block element used to group small sections of text or other elements (bold
or italic text).
2. It will not create a full width block. It stays within the flow of the content.
Use Cases:
1. Apply styles to small part of the text.
Semantic Tags:
1. They are used to provide meaning to the content they wrap.
2. These help search engines and browsers to understand the structure and
purpose of the content
3. It also enhances the SEO (Search Engine Optimization)
SEO = ranking of the webpage on the search engine.
header: defines the header section of the document / webpage
it contains logo, navigation and introductory content
footer: defines the footer section.
it contains information for copyright, privacy policy or contact links
article: self-contained piece of content such as blog post, news article or forum post
it can stand alone and can be distributed independently.
section: defines the thematic grouping, usually with its own heading.
it can be used to group related content within article or webpage.
nav: navigation - it defines a block of navigation what e say as the menu items.
main: Represents the main content of the document.
it is used for the content which is unique to the page excluding the headers
or footers or any sidebars.
figure: content like images or diagrams or charts.
figcaption: which is used to provide a caption or info about the figure or the content
strong: indicates that the text has strong importance. displayed as bold text
em: indicates the strong importance but shown as italic text
Pros of Semantic Tags:
1. SEO improvement - Search engine can understand the content better
2. Accessibility - Screen readers can navigate content more easily
3. Maintainability - Semantic code is easier for developers to read
4. Better User Experience - Clear, organized structure
Forms in HTML
1. User interaction for login, registration, payments or other information gathering
action attribute - defining the control of the form to be moved on submission
method - defining the format of the data to be passed, GET or POST
Form Input Field Types
text - can accept characters and numbers
number - can accept numbers only and also provides option to increment or decrement the values
password - it will mask the input in the format of bullets and provides an option to see the
password in plain text
email - it is used to check if the input is a validate email or not. But the restriction is limited
date - adds a calendar to the field for date selection
file - adds a field to allow the user to upload files from system
Tables - used to present the tabular data
data is displayed into format of cells (row * column)
colspan - extend the occupancy of the cell to multiple columns
rowspan - extend the occupancy of the cell to multiple rows
Task: Create a skeleton for Portfolio page
1. Name, email
2. Work Experience (if any)
3. Your Education Details - display in a tabular format
4. A simple form taking input as an email
